record.paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
record.context_brief: Critical growth index for pinning and unpinning
record.original_question: For quenched-disorder KPZ equations on uniformly growing domains whose propagation velocity scales like t^γ, does γ = 1 play a critical role in the dynamics by separating interfaces that are always pinned for γ < 1 from interfaces that are always moving for γ > 1, or does pinning/unpinning still depend on model parameter values? If parameter dependence remains, are there other critical values of the growth index γ?

evidence.quote: Something similar happens in equation (41): for values of F smaller than a critical one Fc the interface becomes pinned, while for larger values the interface propagates [5].

Note that, contrary to the classical case in which the interface pr opagates linearly in time, in this case the velocity of propagation would be ∼ tγ. It would be interesting to clarify whether γ = 1 plays a critical role in the dynamics or not. In other words, wheth er the interface is always pinned for γ < 1 and always moving for γ > 1, or if there is a dependence on the parameters values in these cases too. If the second situat ion held, it would be yet necessary to clarify whether there are other possible critical valu es for γ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) equation with quenched disorder posed on a uniformly growing spatial domain. Concretely, let h(x,t) denote the height of an interface satisfying

  ∂_t h(x,t) = ν Δh(x,t) + (λ/2) |∇h(x,t)|^2 + F + η(x,h),

where ν,λ>0, F is a constant driving force, and η(x,h) is a quenched random field (time-independent, depending on the spatial position x and on the local height h). The spatial domain on which the equation is posed grows uniformly in time so that its linear size L(t) ~ t^γ for some growth exponent γ>0; equivalently, in comoving coordinates the propagation velocity scales like t^γ rather than being constant.

For the classical case of a static domain, it is known that there is a critical driving force F_c such that for F<F_c the interface is pinned (asymptotically immobile) and for F>F_c the interface propagates. On a uniformly growing domain, address the following:

(a) Does the value γ = 1 play a critical role in the depinning dynamics, in the sense that for every choice of model parameters (ν, λ, F, and disorder distribution) the interface is always pinned whenever γ < 1 and always moving whenever γ > 1?

(b) If, instead, the pinned/moving outcome continues to depend on the parameters (in particular on F relative to F_c) for γ in some range, determine whether there exist other critical values of the growth exponent γ at which a transition between always-pinned, parameter-dependent, and always-moving regimes occurs, and identify such values.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned recent work on quenched KPZ depinning (e.g., 2022 and 2025 arXiv preprints on QKPZ universality and depinning in fractional Brownian landscapes), but none directly addresses the role of a uniform domain-growth exponent γ in separating always-pinned from always-moving regimes for the quenched KPZ equation. No source could be located that resolves whether γ=1 is critical or identifies other critical values of γ, so the status remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Depinning in the quenched Kardar-Parisi-Zhang class I
status_evidence.snippet: Studies depinning transitions in QKPZ via mappings and simulations on static domains.
status_evidence.claim: Recent QKPZ depinning work focuses on static domains, not on growing domains with t^γ velocity scaling.

status_evidence.title: Exponents and front fluctuations in the quenched KPZ universality class
status_evidence.snippet: Determination of critical exponents in QKPZ universality class.
status_evidence.claim: Recent QKPZ literature addresses scaling exponents but not the role of a domain-growth index γ.

status_evidence.title: Depinning of KPZ Interfaces in Fractional Brownian Landscapes
status_evidence.snippet: KPZ depinning in correlated random landscapes.
status_evidence.claim: Variants of KPZ depinning are studied, but the specific question on growth exponent γ is not addressed.
